html: The Nehalem were the northernmost division of the Tillamook, a Salishan-speaking people of the northern Oregon coast, living along the Nehalem River and bay. They fished salmon, gathered shellfish and berries, lived in cedar plank houses and traded with the Chinook and Clatsop near the mouth of the Columbia. Diseases brought by traders from the late 1700s cut their numbers sharply. The treaties they signed in 1851 were never ratified, and most survivors were later gathered on the Siletz or Grand Ronde reservations. The southernmost Tillamook division was the Siletz.
